root_cause: The ArrowRight keydown handler prevents default focus movement and activates the next tab via show(), but does not move keyboard focus to the newly activated tab. After deactivation the previous tab receives tabindex='-1', leaving focus nowhere and causing it to fall back to the body element.
repair_strategy: Insert a call to element.focus() in the _activate method's complete callback, immediately after setting aria-selected=true, so that the newly activated tab receives focus as soon as it becomes active.
expected_accessibility_effect: Arrow key navigation will move focus to the adjacent tab, making it both selected and focused, fulfilling keyboard operability and logical focus order for tablist widgets.
functional_risks: If a tab element is not natively focusable (e.g., a div with role=tab but no tabindex), calling focus() may fail silently or cause unexpected scrolling.
Duplicate focus attempts could occur if other scripts also focus the tab during activation, but this is unlikely.
The change only affects the activation path; deactivation and mouse interactions remain unchanged.
verification_requirements: Press ArrowRight from the Account tab: focus moves to the Notifications tab and aria-selected becomes true.
Press ArrowRight from the Notifications tab: focus moves to the Billing tab and aria-selected becomes true.
Press ArrowLeft (or Shift+ArrowRight) to verify reverse direction focus movement.
Ensure that tab panels update visibility correctly when focus changes via arrow keys.
Confirm that initial tab remains focusable when active and that pressing Tab moves focus into the tabpanel as expected.
